description: Software for publication "Coupled time series of electricity demand, occupancy, weather, and thermal demand for residential buildings is a model or code deposit deposited in Zenodo by its authors Markus Doepfert, Maximiliano Fernando Escobar Viegas (Technical University of Munich). A pluggable Python pipeline that derives coupled hourly residential electricity, occupancy, weather, and heating/cooling time series from any combination of measured load profiles, building archetypes, and historical weather. Released alongside one example instantiation (Germany 2010, ~3.3 M building-year simulations) and three thermal-model classes (1R1C, 5R1C ISO 13790, 7R2C VDI 6007). Coverage: national (DE); the metadata date the deposit to 2026. The formats are not stated in the metadata. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is MIT. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related record: the repository-level record data-zenodo-repository.
